source: She's dead as earth. Lend me a looking-glass!
If that her breath will mist or stain the stone--
Why then, she lives.
Look on her. Look, her lips. Look there, look there.
Oh... oh... oh...
He wasn't in his right mind. Not at the end.
Hamlet, we need to act. Now.
People are dying by Ophelia's hand. She's not sane. I'm not even particularly convinced she's still human.
Fight back? You mean-- kill Ophelia?
She's an imminent threat to all of us.
No. I can't do that. It wouldn't come to that.
Allow me to speak with her. Get her to see reason.
Whatever mystics are taking place here, she's at the center of them, and she can make them cease.
I hope for all of our sakes that you're right.
Just-- be prepared to take swift action if it comes to that.
I'll bring an end to this. One way or another.
Uncle. Thank you for agreeing to meet me.
Of course, of course. What's this about, Hamlet?
I have just one question to ask.
Of course. Anything.
I know you killed him. I have proof. A trusted witness.
All I want to know is, why?
Killed who? I don't know what you mean.
Don't play me for a fool. I know you took my father's life. I know with certainty.
I have no intentions of telling anyone else. But I wanted to hear the truth from you.
I knew this day might come. But I didn't know when.
Perhaps in my heart I've been quietly praying for you to know the truth.
Have mercy, Hamlet. I killed him. But I live with the weight of a regret so deep I cannot touch the bottom.
I have punished myself enough for my crime.
I know it was wrong to have done it. I know it now with everything in my soul.
If... If you have only a shred of mercy within your heart, cling to that, and let it fill you.
It would bear you a rich reward.
We could rule together. You could be Prince not only in name, but in act and deed.
The country would love you for it. Can you imagine? And with my expertise on the throne now, I'd be able to tutor you.
Preparing you for the day when you would become King yourself.
Yes, that's how I could make this right, I think. Restore you to where you ought to be. Where my brother would've wanted you.
You're saying... you... you really did kill him?
I-- find your offer intriguing. I think that would ease Father's spirit, knowing I was preparing to take his place.
Yes. Let me contemplate the offer.
You truly mean it?
Oh, my boy, my poor nephew. I cannot apologize enough.
I need a night's time to think it over, and to pray. We'll speak further after that.
Of course, of course! Anything you desire. Anything at all!
First, I want you to do one thing. I've witnessed my father's spirit, Uncle. I spoke to it.
You see Father's portrait there on the wall?
It's strange. I've not seen it in the gallery in months. He looked so cruel, there.
My brother was a stern man, but the cruelty he earned from our own father.
What would you say to him?
I... I'd say...
Why, there's so much to say.
...How... much I miss...
I don't give a damn.
You and your apologies can burn in hell.
I loved my father with all my heart. As did his country. And you took him from all of us.
No peace-offering of power can bring him back from the dead—or save your soul.
At last. At last. He is justly served.
Ophelia. A word in private, please.
I can scarcely believe it.
I just wish I knew what Father would say.
And Mother, her life-- she was caught up in all this.
Would that she still lived.
(Poor Gertrude. She didn't deserve that.)
I never thought I'd make it this long. I thought...
Everything was so dark for so long. I couldn't feel, couldn't think.
All I wanted to do was die. Some part of me still does.
I know. But now you've got to make the hardest decision of your life.
Where do you go from here, now that you've chosen to live?
I think I already know.
I suppose my betrothal to Brit is something I ought to honor.
That's what a good King does, is it not? Honors his word. Much as I might despise the thought of spending my life with her.
You spoke earlier to me of revisiting things. Seeing them through new eyes.
I've spent these long months trying to purge you from my mind, but I couldn't do it.
All the same, I know you've despised me from afar all summer. I wanted to respect that boundary.
If it's true that you love me no longer, I'll go, and I'll never trouble you again with my affections, nor stumble blindly into your room at dawn.
What will the others say, Hamlet?
Don't you think I saw the way your uncle looked at me, as though I were an annoying insect?
But he's gone now, Ophelia. He's dead.
Listen. I am Prince of this country. And soon, God willing, I will be King. What could you desire that would be beyond my power to control?
But it doesn't have to be. Not anymore.
Is that still something of interest to you?
Revisiting our relationship, you mean?
Do you want me still?
I... was vile to you. I knew it even then. I've done things to you that would shame my father, were he still alive.
No amount of apology can ever remove what I've done to you.
But despite all that, I am deeply, truly, eternally sorry for things I said and did to you.
And—if you can find it in your heart to—ever think of me with affection—
When I was on board our ship to England, Lady Guildenstern took me aside.
You recall that altercation on the boat. It gave me much to think about.
I have failed you many a time, I think. More deeply than I will ever understand.
She explained to me that there are ways in which I have failed the women in my life.
Hamlet, what you did to me was wrong.
You tried to wound me with everything you had. You came after me again and again. And it hurt.
I don't know that I can ever trust you again after that. Or whether you deserve my trust.
With my uncle's passing, I have come to believe in a world of fundamental justice.
Justice for all who have been wronged. Including you.
And in a just world, I'd treat you as my partner and better for the rest of our lives.
The mistakes of our pasts teach us where those whom we love deserve to be.
And you—you deserve to rule Denmark at my side. You'd be a magnificent Queen. I've always said as much, even in my cruelest moments.
Can you share that vision with me? Can you trust me again?
Rekindle my relationship with Hamlet?

source: Hmm. Your mother would be thrilled, I'm certain.
So? Your answer?
I don't forgive you, Hamlet. Not yet. But—
I suspect something in me misses you, after all.
I, ah...
Why are you crying? Isn't this what you wanted?
No, no. It's not that.
These last few days have been-- these last few months have been a living hell.
I couldn't agree more.
Are you afraid of what comes next?
More than I've ever been.
No one is certain what the chain of command ought to be.
I intend to take advantage of that ambiguity. It's time I sat the throne.
What's your plan?
I don't have one. Not yet.
If only there were someone who could give me advice. Help me through this.
I might have some ideas.
Where are you going? Will I see you tonight?
Don't be afraid, Hamlet. The future belongs to you.
Allow me to put thought to action on your behalf.
Until we meet again.
You know, Ophelia, you and I are a tree grown together under the soil. We always have been.
We may come apart, but our trunks rejoin eventually. Even if it's not in love.
My feelings for you will always linger. But sensations other than affection grow stronger. Respect. Admiration.
I'll find my own path. I'm sorry I pushed myself onto you once more.
I need rest. But every time I close my eyes, all I can see are the bloodied faces of two men buried under the earth.
My uncle. My father. And it all feels so empty, like the bottom's fallen out of the world.
I feel so alone.
The dawn will come. I promise.
Where are you going?
Leaving you be for now. I've got to go.
I'm afraid, Ophelia.
Now that your uncle's passed?
Aye. No one is certain what the chain of command ought to be right now.
Will I see you tonight?
Perhaps. Don't be afraid, Hamlet. The future belongs to you.
Hmm. Your mother would be thrilled, I'm certain...
I forgive you, Hamlet.
But I cannot love you the way you've loved me.
I ah... oh.
I'll be the first to admit it, though. I am well and truly afraid.
I intend to take advantage of that ambiguity and extinguish my fear, though. It's time I sat the throne.
Everything all right?
It's as if nothing's changed.
He's dead. And all moves on without him.
Though surely, I know my mother grieves him.
How quickly the loss of a King and Queen is recoverable.
Perhaps... the moment after one's King has been taken is a quiet one.
The game is over, and must be started anew.
And now I line myself up on the edge of the board, ready to fight in his stead.
This should be a moment of triumph for you.
This is what your father wanted, isn't it?
You've eliminated the fox from your hen-house. Murder has been answered with its own kind.
Come, now! Isn't that cause for celebration?
My father is still dead.
I thought Claudius's death would make it all feel right. But it doesn't. It's exactly the same, and now somehow worse.
I never wanted to be King.
And I'm going to fail them all. How long will it take them to realize what an idiot I am, if they haven't yet?
How useless I am—no less a pretender than my uncle—
Hamlet. Look at me.
Chin up.
That's a good lad. Now—deep breath.
A big one.
There. I see a little color in your cheeks.
Feeling any better?
...I don't deserve you, really.
I know. And yet, here I am.
The road before you is a difficult one.
But it is one many men have trodden before you, and will tread after you are gone. You can do this. I promise it.
I have everlasting faith in you, in the goodness that lies within your frail little heart.
And if you cannot believe in your own heart, believe in my good taste, at least.
You need to face this head-on. And you shall. In a scant few days' time, when all this has passed, you will go before the nobility and ask their vote to wear the crown.
If you can find it within you to be ready for that day... then you will make a great King.
...My thanks.
You're right. The time has come to put aside childish things.
